baer_heitev.en: Seven. See Turei Zahav and Magen Avraham, who emended Tosafos, page 3a, s.v. lo nitzrechah: "It is not a refutation, etc., for perhaps it was very long, but it was not seven handbreadths wide, etc." See there, for it must read: "and it was only seven wide." See there. This is straightforward. See Yad Aharon and Responsa Chacham Tzvi, siman 142. The Magen Avraham wrote: It appears to me that even in a very large sukkah, if in one place there is one corner drawn inward that does not have seven, it is forbidden to sit there, since the place is too narrow for him to sit there. See there.

biur_halacha.he:
סוכה שאין בה שבעה וכו' - עיין מ"ב מש"כ בשם המגן אברהם דאם במקום אחד יש קרן וכו'. והנה בבגדי ישע ובבכורי יעקב פקפקו מאוד על ראיתו מקיטוניות דשאני התם דקיטוניות הוא חדר בפ"ע והמחיצה מפסקת ורק שפתוח לסוכה גדולה משא"כ הכא שאין חלוק כלל אפשר דנתבטל לגבי סוכה גדולה [והנה מה דהביא בבכורי יעקב דא"כ לדברי המגן אברהם הא דמכשרינן בסי' זה סוכה עגולה כשיש לרבע בתוכה ז' על ז' צריך לכוון לישב דוקא באמצעה ממש באותו מקום שיש לרבע ז' על ז' דמן הצד שמצר והולך אין בו זע"ז ויש לו דין הקרן לדעת המגן אברהם [ועיין במה שכתב הדה"ח ואעתיק דבריו לקמיה] ולענ"ד לא דמי זה לזה דשם הולך כל העיגול מבפנים בשטח אחד ואין לחלק זה מזה וכולו כשר דאין צר לו לשבת שם כלל דשטח אחד הוא עם הריבוע ולכן לא אישתמיט אחד מן האחרונים לחלק בזה משא"כ בענינינו אף דאין מחיצה מפסקת מ"מ הרי מנכר שהקרן הזה חלוק מן הסוכה הגדולה וצר לו לשבת בקרן ההוא ולכן מחמיר המגן אברהם בזה] והנה בדה"ח ראיתי שהעתיק ג"כ דברי המגן אברהם וסיים ע"ז ודוקא כשהקרן אינו רחב ז' ג"כ אבל כשהקרן רחב ז' רק אינו ארוך ז' כשר כיון שמצורף לסוכה גדולה תדע דהא בעגול ויש לרבע ז' על ז' מותר לישב סמוך להדופן אף דבעגולה סמוך לדופן ליכא זע"ז א"ו כיון דמצורף לגדולה כשר דבשלמא כשהקרן אינו רחב ז' ג"כ יש לומר דחשיב כלול של תרנגולים כמש"כ רש"י ותוספות ופסולה אבל כשרחב ז' רק שאינו ארוך ז' ודאי דכשרה דמצורף לסוכה גדולה מידי דהוי אם ראשו ורובו בסוכה קטנה ושולחנו בסוכה גדולה כנ"ל עכ"ל והנה ראייתם מסוכה עגולה כבר דחינו ומה שכתב מידי דהוי אם ראשו ורובו בסוכה קטנה כו' תמיה גדולה דזה אינו כשר רק לשיטת הרי"ף דסוכה שמחזקת רק ראשו ורובו בסוכה ושולחנו בתוך הבית אינו מיפסל רק מדרבנן משום גזירה שמא ימשך אחר שלחנו ובזה ששולחנו בתוך הסוכה הגדולה ליכא למיגזר כלל [אבל לא משום דמצטרף הקטנה לגדולה כסברתו] אבל לדעת הר"ן וסייעתו דסוכה קטנה שמחזקת רק ראשו ורובו [והוא כוי"ו על וי"ו] יש בה עצם הפסול דלאו דירה היא כלל ופסולה מן התורה בודאי לא יצא ידי חובתו האוכל בה אף כששולחנו בתוך הגדולה וכמו שכתב בתור"ע והמ"א הלא כל דבריו הוא רק להר"ן. ולענ"ד דינא דמ"א דמיא למאי דאמרינן בשבת דף ז' דקרן זוית הסמוכה לר"ה כיון דלא ניחא תשמישתיה אינו מצטרף עם הר"ה אף דליכא הפסק ביניהן וככרמלית דמיא וה"נ כיון דצר לו לשבת שם. ומדברי המגן אברהם משמע ג"כ דלא כוותיה שכתב שאין בו ז' על ז' ונמשך במאמר אחד עם הקודם משמע דדינו כשאר סוכה שאין בה ז' באורך וז' ברוחב דפסולה וע"כ לפענ"ד אין לזוז מדברי המגן אברהם אכן בפרט אחד נראה דיש להקל בזה וכמו שכתב בבכורי יעקב וז"ל אף שלא מלאני לבי להקל לישב שם נגד דעת המגן אברהם מ"מ נ"ל שא"צ להקפיד שלא להניח השולחן באותו קרן ולא חיישינן בזה שמא ימשך אחר שולחנו כיון שהרבה פוסקים ס"ל דאפילו בשולחנו בתוך הבית לא גזרינן הכי כדאי הם לסמוך עליהם בזה. ודע עוד דהא דבעינן השיעור ז' על ז' הוא בכל גובה עשרה טפחים כדלעיל בסימן תרל"א סעיף יו"ד בהג"ה ועיין בפמ"ג דצריך הכל בריבוע ונוי סוכה דממעטין מן הצד הוא ג"כ עד גובה י"ט ועיין לקמיה בס"ג מש"כ שם:
פסולה - עיין ברא"ש הטעם דלראשו ורובו של אדם צריך אמה דגברא באמתה יתיב ושולחנו מחזיק טפח וכ"כ הריטב"א והנה ידוע המחלוקת שיש בין הראשונים דלהרי"ף שפסק כב"ש בתרתי משום דחד טעמא הוא לתרוייהו הא דאסרינן במחזקת ראשו ורובו ושולחנו בתוך הבית הוא ג"כ רק משום גזירה שמא ימשך אחר שולחנו כמו שביאר הר"ן לדבריו ולפ"ז מן התורה די בראשו ורובו בלבד והוא שיעור וי"ו על וי"ו ורבנן תקנו ז' על ז' כדי שיוכל להעמיד השולחן בתוך הסוכה ולא ימשך אחריו וליתר הפוסקים כל שאין בו ז' על ז' שיוכל להיות שם ראשו ורובו אין בו הכשר סוכה מן התורה דלאו דירה היא כלל כמו שכתב הר"ן וק"ק לי על דברי הפמ"ג שכתב דסוכה שאין בה ז' על ז' פסולה מן התורה וראשו ורובו בסוכה גדולה ושולחנו בתוך הבית הוא אסור רק משום גזירה שמא ימשך אחר שולחנו ולענ"ד ארכביה אתרי רכשי דמאן דאית ליה במחזקת רק ראשו ורובו דפסולו מן התורה לית ליה הגזירה כלל ביושב בסוכה גדולה ושולחנו בתוך הבית כמבואר בר"ן ויתר הפוסקים ומאן דאית ליה הך גזירה לדידיה בסוכה שמחזקת רק ראשו ורובו ושולחנו בתוך הבית פסולו הוא רק מדרבנן כנ"ל [וגם מה שכתב דכל שאין ז' על ז' מה"ת פסולה דהוא הלמ"מ ג"כ לא נהירא דידוע מה שכתב הרמב"ם דבהלכה למ"מ אין בה מחלוקת ובזה פליגי ב"ש וב"ה כדאיתא בגמרא] ואולי לדעת הרמב"ן שהבאתי בשער הציון משמע קצת מיניה דהוא סבר דגם לדעת הרי"ף הוא דאורייתא ויותר נראה שסמך בזה על לשון הרמב"ם פ"ד מהלכות סוכה ה"א שכתב היתה פחותה מעשרה או מז' על ז' או גבוה מכ' אמה וכו' הרי שכלל זה בכל פסולי דאורייתא ומ"מ דעתו בפ"ז הלכה ח' דגזרינן גם בגדולה היכי ששולחנו בתוך הבית:
biur_halacha.en:
A sukkah that does not have seven, etc. See Mishnah Berurah, where I wrote in the name of the Magen Avraham that if in one place there is a corner, etc. Now, in Bigdei Yesha and Bikkurei Yaakov they strongly questioned his proof from the small chambers, for there it is different, since a small chamber is a room by itself and the partition separates it, except that it opens into a large sukkah. Here, by contrast, where there is no division at all, perhaps it is nullified to the large sukkah. [Now, regarding what Bikkurei Yaakov brought, that if so, according to the Magen Avraham, when we validate in this siman a round sukkah that has enough space to square within it seven by seven, one would have to be careful to sit specifically in its exact center, in that place where there is enough to square seven by seven, for at the side, where it narrows progressively, there is not seven by seven and it should have the law of the corner according to the Magen Avraham. See what the Derech HaChayim wrote, and I will quote his words below. In my humble opinion the two cases are not comparable, for there the entire circle proceeds inside as one surface, and one cannot divide one part from another; all of it is valid, since it is not at all too narrow for him to sit there, for it is one surface with the square. Therefore none of the later authorities failed to distinguish this. But in our case, even though no partition separates it, nevertheless it is recognizable that this corner is divided from the large sukkah, and it is too narrow for him to sit in that corner; therefore the Magen Avraham is stringent in this.] Now, I saw in Derech HaChayim that he also copied the words of the Magen Avraham, and he concluded about this: specifically when the corner is also not seven wide; but when the corner is seven wide, only it is not seven long, it is valid, since it is joined to the large sukkah. Know this from the fact that with a circle that has enough to square seven by seven, one may sit near the wall, even though in a round sukkah near the wall there is not seven by seven. Rather, perforce, since it is joined to the large one, it is valid. For granted, when the corner is also not seven wide, one can say that it is considered like a chicken coop, as Rashi and Tosafos wrote, and is invalid; but when it is seven wide, only not seven long, it is certainly valid, for it is joined to the large sukkah, just as in the case where his head and most of him are in a small sukkah and his table is in a large sukkah. These are his words. Now, we have already rejected their proof from a round sukkah. And what he wrote, "just as in the case where his head and most of him are in a small sukkah, etc.," is very astonishing, for that is valid only according to the Rif's approach, that a sukkah which holds only his head and most of him in the sukkah while his table is inside the house is invalid only rabbinically, because of the decree lest he be drawn after his table; and when his table is inside the large sukkah there is no concern for such a decree at all [but not because the small sukkah joins to the large one, as he reasoned]. But according to the Ran and those who support him, that a small sukkah which holds only his head and most of him [and it is six by six] has an intrinsic disqualification, for it is not a dwelling at all and is invalid by Torah law, one certainly has not fulfilled his obligation when eating in it, even when his table is inside the large one, as the Tosafos Rabbi Akiva Eiger wrote. And all the Magen Avraham's words are only according to the Ran. In my humble opinion the law of the Magen Avraham is comparable to what we say in Shabbos 7, that a corner adjacent to the public domain, since its use is inconvenient, does not join with the public domain, even though there is no separation between them, and it is like a karmelis. So too here, since it is too narrow for him to sit there. The Magen Avraham's words also imply unlike him, for he wrote "which does not have seven by seven," and it continues in one statement with the preceding matter, implying that its law is like any other sukkah that does not have seven in length and seven in width, which is invalid. Therefore, in my humble opinion one should not move from the words of the Magen Avraham. However, in one particular it seems that one may be lenient, as Bikkurei Yaakov wrote: "Although my heart has not emboldened me to be lenient to sit there against the view of the Magen Avraham, nevertheless it appears to me that one need not be careful not to place the table in that corner, and we are not concerned here lest he be drawn after his table, since many poskim hold that even when his table is inside the house we do not decree so; they are worthy to rely upon in this matter." Know further that the requirement of the measure of seven by seven applies throughout a height of ten handbreadths, as above in siman 631:10 in the gloss. See Pri Megadim, that everything must be squared, and sukkah decorations that reduce the space from the side also do so up to a height of ten handbreadths. See below in se'if 3 what I wrote there.
Is invalid. See the Rosh for the reason: for the head and most of a person an amah is needed, since a person sits within an amah, and his table occupies one handbreadth. So wrote the Ritva as well. Now, the dispute among the early authorities is known. According to the Rif, who ruled like Beis Shammai in both matters because one reason applies to both, the reason we prohibit a sukkah that holds his head and most of him while his table is inside the house is also only because of the decree lest he be drawn after his table, as the Ran explained his view. According to this, by Torah law his head and most of him alone is enough, and that is a measure of six by six; the Sages enacted seven by seven so that he can place the table inside the sukkah and not be drawn after it. But according to the other poskim, whenever it does not have seven by seven, so that his head and most of him can be there, it does not have the status of a valid sukkah by Torah law, for it is not a dwelling at all, as the Ran wrote. I have some difficulty with the words of Pri Megadim, who wrote that a sukkah which does not have seven by seven is invalid by Torah law, and that when his head and most of him are in a large sukkah while his table is inside the house, it is prohibited only because of the decree lest he be drawn after his table. In my humble opinion he has mounted two steeds at once, for the one who holds that when it holds only his head and most of him its invalidity is by Torah law does not hold of the decree at all when one sits in a large sukkah and his table is inside the house, as is explicit in the Ran and the other poskim; and the one who holds of this decree holds that a sukkah that holds only his head and most of him while his table is inside the house is invalid only rabbinically, as above. [Also what he wrote, that anything without seven by seven is invalid by Torah law because it is a law given to Moshe at Sinai, is also not clear, for the Rambam's statement is known that there is no dispute about a law given to Moshe at Sinai, whereas here Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel disagree, as stated in the Gemara.] Perhaps according to the Ramban, whom I brought in Sha'ar HaTziyun, it is somewhat implied that he held that even according to the Rif it is Torah law. More likely, he relied in this on the language of the Rambam, chapter 4 of Hilchos Sukkah, halachah 1, who wrote: if it was lower than ten, or less than seven by seven, or higher than twenty amos, etc.; thus he included this with all disqualifications that are by Torah law. Nevertheless, in chapter 7, halachah 8, his view is that we decree even in a large sukkah when his table is inside the house.

machatzit_hashekel.he:
(ס"ק א) ז' על ז' כו' עכ"ל רש"י דף ב' ע"ב. אע"פ שהיא ארוכה הרב' ואם יחתכנה לרצועות תמצא בה מ"ט רצועות שיהי' כ"א טפח על טפח. שהוא שיעור ז' על ז' שיש בו ג"כ מ"ט רצועות שהן טפח על טפח. וכ"מ סעיף ב' שכתב שצריך להיות בו כדי לרבע כו' משמ' שצריך שיהי' רבוע של ז' על ז' בתוך העיגול. ולא מהני במה שאפשר לחתוך רצועות מן העיגול שיעלו מ"ט וכ"א טפח על טפח:
והב"ח נדחק עצמו בטור שכתב ג"כ כלשון זה גבי סכה עגולה ויש בה כדי לרבע ז' על ז' עכ"ל:
וכ"כ התוס' דף ג' כו' זה ראיית הב"ח דאי' ריש סכה לכמה אמוראי הא דפליגי ר"י ורבנן בסכ' שהיא גבוה למעל' מכ' אמה. דרבנן פסלי ור"י מכשיר. פליגי בכל גווני בין שתהי' רחבה הרב' או כשיעור מצומצם. אלא דרב הונא אמר רב דל"פ אלא בסכ' שהיא ד' אמות על ד"א. אבל בגדול' יותר מזה מודו רבנן דכשרה ורב חנן בר רבא אמר רב דלא פליגי רק באינ' מחזקת אלא ראשו ורובו ושלחנו. אבל בגרול' יותר מזה מודו רבנן דכשרה. ופריך הש"ס מדתני' א"ל ר"י לרבנן מעש' בהילני המלכ' שהית' יושבת בסכה גבוה יותר מכ' וגם שבעה בניה ישבו עמה. ולא אמרו לה רבנן דבר וניהו דאשה פטור' מ"מ ה"ל לרבנן למונעה משום ז' בניה בשלמא לאמוראי דפליגי בכל גווני בין בסכה גדולה ובין בקטנה שפיר אלא למ"ד דוקא בסכה קטנה פליגי וכי דרכה של מלכה לישב בשכה קטנה. ואי גדולה הוי הא מודו רבנן דכשרה ומאי ראי' מייתי ר"י לדבדיו ומשני שסכה גדול' הי' לה לצורך בני ביתה אלא שהסכ' גדולה הית' פתוחה לקיטונית. דהיינו סכות קטנות והיו גבוהים יותר מכ' והלני משום צניעות ישבה בקיטונית. ובהא פליגי דרבנן סברו דבניה בגדול' היו יושבים. והיא שישבה בקיטונית והית' גבוה יותר מכ'. מה בכך הא אשה פטור' מן הסכ' ור"י סבר בניה אצלה היו יושבים בקיטונית והיו הבנים חייביש בסכה ואפ"ה לא אמרו לה דבר ע"כ צריך לומר דלמעל' מכ' כשרה. והקשה רש"י דאכתי תיקשי לר' חנן ב"ר דס"ל דל"פ אלא באינה מחזקת אלא כדי ראשו ורובו ושלחנו. אם כן איך א"ל דבניה גבי דידה היו יושבים. וכי אפשר לישב ת' בני אדם בסכה שאינה מחזקת אלא כדי ראשו ורובו ושלחנו של אדם א'. וע"ז תי' התוס' דהית' ארוכ' הרב' ואינה רחבה שבעה טפחים ובניה באותו אורך היו יושבים עכת"ד. הרי אפילו אינה רחבה שבע' מכל מקום כיון דהית' ארוכה הרב' כשרה. דאפשר לעשות ממנה מ"ט רצועות וכ"א טפח מ"ש:
דפשוט דט"ס. וכמו שכתב הט"ז דממ"נ אי כוונות התוספות שהית' ארוכה הרב' ר"ל יותר מז' טפחים עד שיעלה אם תחתכנה לרצועות יהי' בהן מ"ט רצועות וכ"א טפח ע"ט. אכתי תיקשי האיך אפשר לח' בני אדם לישב בסכה כזו. כיון דעכ"פ איננה מחזקת בצירוף כ"א כדי ראשו ורובו ושלחנו של אדם א' ואי כוונחם שהית' ארוכה מאד ואם תחתכנה יעלה יותר ממ"ט רצועות של טפח ע"ט. ולכן הי' אפשר שבניה' אצלה היו יושבים. מ"מ מי דחקם שלא הית' רחבה ז"ט אפי' הית' רחב' ז"ט מ"מ אפשר שהית' ארוכה הרב' כיון דבלא"ה צ"ל דהית' מחזקת יותר מז' על ז' אע"כ צ"ל הגרסא ולא הית' רחבה אלא שבע' טפחים וא"כ שפיר י"ל דהית' ארוכה הרב' עד שהית' מחזקת הרב' יותר משיעור ז' על ז"ט:
דהא קאי אדברי רש"י ורבנן ור' יוד' כצ"ל. ר"ל דהם מיירי ברחבה ז"ט ולא שינוי התוס' וכתבו דלא הית' רחבה ז'. כיון דבלא"ה ע"כ צ"ל שהית' מחזקת יותר משיעור ז' על ז' כנ"ל:
ואדרבא מוכח משם כו' מדכתבו שלא הית' רחבה אלא ז'. והוא ללא צורך דליישב קושייתם הי' מספיק אם היו מתרצי' שהית' ארוכה הרב'. אלא כתבו כן להוציא מסברת הב"ח. ך"ח טפחים וב"ח כיון דמרובע בעי' ז' על ז' א"כ האלכסון שעולה ב' חומשין יותר כפי הכלל כל אמתא בריבוע אמתא וב"ח באלכסונ' אם כן האלכסון עולה ט' טפחים וד' חומשין. ואם יעשה כזה בעיגול. צריך העיגול להחזיק כל האלכסון של הריבוע. כי בעיגול הכל הוא אלכסון דהיינו ט' טפחים וד"ח. ולפי הכלל כל שיש ברחבו טפח יש בהקיפו ג"ט. א"כ חוט המקיף את העיגול הוא ג' פעמים ט' טפחים וד"ח. וזה עולה ד"ט טפחים וב"ח:
ומ"ש הב"ח מ"ש ממזוזה כצ"ל. והיינו לרמב"ם (וט"ס יש בב"ח ונתחלף הרמב"ם ברא"ש) דהיינו אם נאמר דבעי' כאן דוקא רבוע של ז' על ז' ולא מהני אם אינה רחבה ז' וארוכ' הרב'. הא במזוזה:
פליג הרא"ש עם הרמב"ם דהרא"ש ס"ל הא דקי"ל בית שאין בו ד' אמות על ד"א פטור ממזוזה. אם הוא ארוך יותר מד"א ואינו רחב ד"א פטור ממזוזה אע"ג דאם תחתכנו לרצועות תמצא כפי שיעור ד' אמות על ד' אמות. והרמב"ם ס"ל כה"ג חייב במזוזה. אם כן לרמב"ם תיקשי מ"ש דבסכה בעי' השיעור המרובע. והוי סגי בוי"ו על וי"ו:
ול"ד אלא ר"ל פחות מז' על ז':
וכ"מ בגמרא דף ג' בקיטונית. הוא גמרא הנ"ל. ולפי מה שפירש מ"א דברי התו' הנ"ל דהעתיקו דוקא שלא הית' רחבה אלא ז' טפחים דאם הית' קצרה מז' טפחים הית' פסולה. אף ע"ג דארוכה הרב' לאפוקי מדעת הב"ח כנ"ל. ותיקשי ניהו דליתא לדברי הב"ח מ"מ אין צריך שתהי' הקיטונית רחבים ז'. ואפ"ה כשרים מטעם פסל היוצא מן הסוכ'. דהא הקיטונית היו פתוחים לסכה הגדול'. וכמשמעות לשון הש"ס לא נצרכה אלא לקיטונית שבה א"ו צ"ל כדברי מ"א דכה"ג אינו מתכשר משום פסל היוצא מ"ה כיון שהמקום צר לשבת. עוד י"ל ראיית מ"א מדאייתי ר"י ראי' מהילני דס"ל דבניה אצלה היו יושבים בסכה גבוה למעל' מכ'. ומאי ראי' דלמא הוכשרו הקיטונית משום פסל היוצא מ"ה דלמעל' מכ' נכשר ע"י פסל היוצא מ"ה כמ"ש מ"א סי' תרל"ג סעיף קטן ה'. אלא צ"ל דוקא לדידן דטעם למעל' מכ' משום דירת עראי אבל לר' חנן דפליגי רבנן ור"י דוקא באין מחזקת רק ראשו ורובו ושלחנו. דהטעם כמ"ש התוספות דהוי כלול של תרנגולים ע"ש א"כ למעל' מכ' סכך פסול מיקרי ואינו ניתר ע"י פסל היוצא מ"ה. (וכן צ"ל למ"ד דוקא בד"א על ד"א פליגי וטעם הפסול משום דליכא צל סכך מיקרי למעל' מכ' סכך פסול) ומזה למד מ"א לדידן בקרן שאין בו ז' על ז' דאינו נכשר ע"י פסל היוצא מ"ה וראי' זו עיקר:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
(Small paragraph 1) Seven by seven, etc. These are Rashi's words on page 2b: even though it is very long, and if one were to cut it into strips one would find in it forty-nine strips, each one a handbreadth by a handbreadth, which is the measure of seven by seven, for it too contains forty-nine strips that are a handbreadth by a handbreadth. So it is also implied by se'if 2, where he wrote that it must contain enough to square, etc.; this implies that there must be a square of seven by seven within the circle. It does not help that it is possible to cut strips from the circle that total forty-nine, each one a handbreadth by a handbreadth.
The Bach pressed himself regarding the Tur, who also wrote this language with respect to a round sukkah: "and it has enough to square seven by seven." These are his words.
And so Tosafos wrote on page 3, etc. This is the proof of the Bach. It is stated at the beginning of Sukkah, according to several amoraim, that the dispute of Rabbi Yehudah and the Sages regarding a sukkah that is higher than twenty amos, where the Sages invalidate it and Rabbi Yehudah validates it, applies in every manner, whether it is very wide or of an exact minimal measure. But Rav Huna said in the name of Rav that they disagree only about a sukkah that is four amos by four amos; if it is larger than this, the Sages agree that it is valid. And Rav Chanan bar Rabbah said in the name of Rav that they disagree only when it holds only his head, most of him, and his table; but if it is larger than this, the Sages agree that it is valid. The Talmud challenges from a Baraisa: Rabbi Yehudah said to the Sages, there was an incident with Queen Helene, who was sitting in a sukkah higher than twenty, and her seven sons sat with her, and the Sages said nothing to her. Although a woman is exempt, nevertheless the Sages should have stopped her because of her seven sons. Granted, according to the amoraim who say that they disagree in every manner, both in a large sukkah and in a small one, this is fine. But according to the one who says that they disagree specifically in a small sukkah, is it the way of a queen to sit in a small sukkah? And if it was a large one, the Sages agree that it is valid, so what proof did Rabbi Yehudah bring for his words? The Talmud answers that she had a large sukkah for the members of her household, but the large sukkah opened to a small chamber, meaning small sukkos, and they were higher than twenty; Helene, because of modesty, sat in the small chamber. This is the point of their dispute: the Sages held that her sons sat in the large one, and she sat in the small chamber, which was higher than twenty. What of it? A woman is exempt from sukkah. Rabbi Yehudah held that her sons sat with her in the small chamber, and the sons were obligated in sukkah, yet they said nothing to her; therefore one must say that higher than twenty is valid. Rashi asked that it still remains difficult for Rabbi Chanan bar Rabbah, who holds that they disagree only when it holds only his head, most of him, and his table. If so, how can one say that her sons sat with her? Is it possible for eight people to sit in a sukkah that holds only the head, most of him, and table of one person? About this Tosafos answered that it was very long and was not seven handbreadths wide, and her sons sat along that length. These are the contents of their words. Thus, even if it is not seven wide, nevertheless since it was very long it is valid, because it is possible to make from it forty-nine strips, each one a handbreadth. This is what he wrote.
For it is obvious that it is a scribal error. As the Turei Zahav wrote: one way or the other, if Tosafos meant that it was very long, meaning more than seven handbreadths, until, if one cut it into strips, it would contain forty-nine strips, each one a handbreadth by a handbreadth, it would still be difficult: how could eight people sit in such a sukkah, since in any event when joined together it holds only the head, most of him, and table of one person? And if they meant that it was extremely long, so that if it were cut it would yield more than forty-nine strips of a handbreadth by a handbreadth, and therefore her sons could sit with her, nevertheless what forced them to say that it was not seven handbreadths wide? Even if it was seven handbreadths wide, it could still have been very long, since in any case one must say that it held more than seven by seven. Rather, perforce the correct text must be: "and it was only seven handbreadths wide." If so, one can well say that it was very long, until it held much more than the measure of seven by seven handbreadths.
For it is referring to the words of Rashi and the Sages and Rabbi Yehudah; this is the correct reading. That is, they are discussing one that is seven handbreadths wide, and Tosafos did not change this and write that it was not seven wide, since in any case one must say that it held more than the measure of seven by seven, as above.
And on the contrary, it is proven from there, etc. For they wrote that it was only seven wide. This was unnecessary, for to answer their difficulty it would have sufficed had they answered that it was very long. Rather, they wrote this to exclude the reasoning of the Bach. Twenty-eight handbreadths and two fifths: since the Bach holds that we require a square of seven by seven, the diagonal, which is two fifths greater according to the rule that every amah in a square has an amah and two fifths in its diagonal, therefore the diagonal totals nine handbreadths and four fifths. If one makes such a thing in a circle, the circle must contain the entire diagonal of the square, for in a circle the entire matter is the diagonal, meaning nine handbreadths and four fifths. According to the rule that anything with a width of one handbreadth has a circumference of three handbreadths, the cord surrounding the circle is three times nine handbreadths and four fifths. This equals twenty-nine handbreadths and two fifths.
And what the Bach wrote, "why is it different from mezuzah"; this is the correct reading. This refers to the Rambam [and there is a scribal error in the Bach, where Rambam was exchanged with Rosh]. That is, if we say that here we specifically require a square of seven by seven, and it does not help if it is not seven wide but is very long, behold, with respect to mezuzah:
The Rosh disagrees with the Rambam. The Rosh holds that what we rule, that a house which does not have four amos by four amos is exempt from mezuzah, means that if it is longer than four amos but is not four amos wide, it is exempt from mezuzah, even though if one were to cut it into strips one would find the measure of four amos by four amos. The Rambam holds that in such a case it is obligated in mezuzah. If so, according to the Rambam the question is difficult: why, regarding sukkah, do we require the square measure? It should have sufficed with six by six.
It is not exact; rather, he means less than seven by seven.
And so it is implied in the Gemara, page 3, regarding the small chamber. This is the Gemara mentioned above. According to the way the Magen Avraham explained the words of Tosafos mentioned above, that they specifically copied that it was only seven handbreadths wide, for if it was narrower than seven handbreadths it would be invalid even though it was very long, in order to exclude the view of the Bach as above, it is difficult: granted, the Bach's words are not correct, nevertheless the small chambers did not need to be seven wide, and even so they should be valid by reason of "the s'chach that extends from the sukkah," for the small chambers opened to the large sukkah, as implied by the language of the Talmud, "it was necessary only for the small chamber in it." Rather, perforce one must say like the words of the Magen Avraham, that in such a case it is not validated because of "the s'chach that extends from the sukkah," since the place is narrow for sitting. One can also say that the proof of the Magen Avraham is from the fact that Rabbi Yehudah brought proof from Helene, for he held that her sons sat with her in a sukkah higher than twenty. What proof is there? Perhaps the small chambers were validated because of "the s'chach that extends from the sukkah," for an area higher than twenty is validated through "the s'chach that extends from the sukkah," as the Magen Avraham wrote in siman 633, small paragraph 5. Rather, one must say that this applies specifically according to us, where the reason for invalidating higher than twenty is because of a temporary dwelling. But according to Rabbi Chanan, that the Sages and Rabbi Yehudah disagree specifically about one that holds only his head, most of him, and his table, where the reason is, as Tosafos wrote, that it is like a chicken coop; see there. If so, above twenty is called invalid s'chach, and it is not permitted by means of "the s'chach that extends from the sukkah." [And so one must say according to the one who says that they disagree specifically about four amos by four amos, where the reason for invalidity is because there is no shade from the s'chach: above twenty is called invalid s'chach.] From this the Magen Avraham learned regarding our case, a corner that does not have seven by seven, that it is not validated through "the s'chach that extends from the sukkah." This proof is primary.

magen_avraham.he: ז' על ז' בעינן. לפי שדרך סעודתן בהסיב' ואין אוכלי' זקופים ויושבים כמונו לפיכך צריך ז' על ז' שיהא בה ראשו ורובו ושולחנו לאפוקי קטנ' שראשו נכנס בה ושלחנו ולא רובו או ראשו ורובו ולא שלחנו עכ"ל רש"י והרי מבואר דאם היא אינה רחבה אף על פי שארוכ' הרבה פסולה דהא אינה יכול' לישב בה ראשו ורובו ושלחנו וכ"מ מכל הפוסקים וכ"מ בס"ב גבי סוכ' עגול', והב"ח נדחק עצמו וכתב דדעת הטור דאם היא ארוכ' וקצר' כשיר' וכ"כ התו' דף ג' בד"ה לא נצרכה דסוכה ארוכה ואין רחבה ז' כשרה עכ"ל, ולא דק דפשוט דט"ס הוא בתו' וצ"ל ואין רחב' אלא שבע' דהא קאי אדברי רש"י [ור"י] ע"ש דאינהו מיירי ברחבה שבעה ע"ש ואדרב' מוכח משם דמקרי סוכה קטנה והעיקר דסוכה עגולה צריך שיהא בהקיפ' כ' טפחים ושני חומשים ומ"ש [הב"ח] מ"ש ממזוזה דאע"ג דאריך וקטין חייב כמו שכ' בי"ד סי' רפ"ו סי"ג לק"מ דהכא בעי' שישב בה ראשו ורובו ושלחנו כמש"ל ולהכי בעי' מרובע ונ"ל דאפי' לדידן שיושבי' זקופים והוי סגי בו' על ו' מ"מ בעינן ז' על ז' דבציר מזה לאו דיר' היא כלל כמ"ש הר"ן, ונ"ל דאפי' הסוכה גדול' הרבה ובמקום א' יש קרן א' משוך לפנים שאין בו ז' על ז' אסור לישב שם כיון שהמקום צר לו לשבת שם וכ"מ בגמרא דף ג' ע"ש בקיטונית:
magen_avraham.en: We require seven by seven. Because their manner of eating was while reclining, and they did not eat upright and seated as we do, therefore seven by seven is required, so that it contains his head, most of him, and his table, excluding a small one into which his head and table enter but not most of him, or his head and most of him but not his table. These are Rashi's words. It is explicit that if it is not wide, even though it is very long, it is invalid, for he cannot sit in it with his head, most of him, and his table. So it is also implied from all the poskim, and so it is implied in se'if 2 regarding a round sukkah. The Bach pressed himself and wrote that the Tur's view is that if it is long and narrow it is valid, and Tosafos likewise wrote on page 3, s.v. lo nitzrechah, that a long sukkah that is not seven wide is valid. These are his words. But he was not precise, for it is obvious that there is a scribal error in Tosafos, and it must read: "and it was only seven wide," for it is referring to the words of Rashi and Rabbi Yehudah; see there, as they are discussing one that is seven wide. See there. On the contrary, it is proven from there that it is called a small sukkah. The main law is that a round sukkah must have a circumference of twenty-nine handbreadths and two fifths. As for what the Bach wrote, "why is it different from mezuzah, where even though it is long and narrow it is obligated, as written in Yoreh De'ah, siman 286:13," this is not difficult at all, for here we require that he sit in it with his head, most of him, and his table, as written above, and therefore we require a square. It appears to me that even for us, who sit upright and for whom six by six would suffice, nevertheless we require seven by seven, for less than that is not a dwelling at all, as the Ran wrote. It appears to me further that even if the sukkah is very large, but in one place there is a corner drawn inward that does not have seven by seven, it is forbidden to sit there, since the place is too narrow for him to sit there. So it is implied in the Gemara, page 3; see there, regarding the small chamber.

peri_megadim.en: Seven by seven, etc. See Turei Zahav, who agreed with what the Magen Avraham wrote in letter 1, and as the Mechaber wrote in se'if 2, that a round sukkah needs enough space to square seven by seven handbreadths. In Tosafos there, the word "only" should be inserted: "seven by seven handbreadths"; and so wrote the Magen Avraham. See the Rambam, chapter 4, regarding adding several mil to its length. So too the Mechaber wrote. The Bach wrote that there is no concern that it is not a temporary dwelling because one would need to strengthen the walls, for according to Rava this is what is taught; see there. If one placed s'chach over a karpef that was not enclosed for dwelling, it requires analysis whether one may carry on the Shabbos during Sukkos. See siman 630 in the Magen Avraham, letter 9, and examine the Magen Avraham about this. There is a scribal error in the printing, and it should read: "for if it is a handbreadth wide and several handbreadths long, it is obvious that it is not a dwelling, etc." See what I will write, with Hashem's help, in the following letter.

peri_megadim.he: צריך עט״ז האריך ותוכן כוונתו כמ״ש באות א׳ דבעינן בסוכה זעז״ט לרבא ממש לא ע״י צירוף והיינו דנפיק ריבועא מיגו עיגולא זעז״ט ומה שעודף העיגול מריבוע אין מצטרף כלל וכמו לר׳ יוחנן בסוכה ח׳ א׳ בעי כך ד״א על ד״א ה״ה לדידן עב״ח ז״ל. ובי״ד רפ״ו סי״ג ועש״ך אות כ״ג המחבר שם פסק דמצטרף שפיר מה שבצדדין בעיגול ואם יש בין הכל שם לרבע ד״א חייב במזוזה אפילו שאין ריבוע מגו עיגולא כהרמב״ם שם דלא כהרא״ש דסבר גם שם ריבוע מגו עיגולא ממש בעינן ועמ״א כאן אות א׳ דלא תקשה דברי הש״ע אהדדי דכאן בסוכה בעינן שישב ראשו ורובו ושלחנו א״א בלי ריבוע ממש משא״כ בסוכה ד״א על ד״א בין הכל ע״י צירוף סגי להר״מ ז״ל לפי דעת הרא״ש והב״י. וע״ש בדפוס במ״א רש״י צ״ל הב״ח והיינו כפי מה שהבין הרא״ש בהר״מ ל״ק מ״ש סוכה ממזוזה וכאמור. ע׳ בסי׳ תרל״א במ״א אות י׳ דצריך זעז״ט בגובה י״ט משמע הכל בריבוע ונוי סוכה דממעטין מהצד ה״ה בגובה י״ט ממעטין זעז״ט מהצד כל גובה י״ט וצ״ע בכל הני אי מ״ה פסולה סוכה כה״ג או מדרבנן עסי׳ תרכ״ט במ״א אות כ״ב וע׳ גמ׳ סוכה י׳ ב׳ שלוחי מצוה אנו ופטורין מסוכה ועתוס׳ ועח״ר שם ויראה דלמ״ד נוי סוכה המופלגין ד״ט פסולה מדרבנן ומש״ה חשיב להו כשעת הדחק וכאין להם סוכה אחרת מש״ה ישבו שם וברוכי נמי מברכי למ״ש בחה״ר בהא דאין שעת הסכנה ראיה אבל אם היה פסולה מ״ה לא היו ישנים שם דמה נ״מ בה א״נ הואיל ופלוגתא הוא אחמרו אנפשייהו מיהת והבן זה ונ״מ לדינא בזה וכדאמרן:
peri_megadim.en: It must. See Turei Zahav, who discussed this at length, and the content of his intent is as I wrote in letter 1: that in a sukkah we require an actual seven by seven handbreadths according to Rava, not through combining parts. That is, the square that emerges from within the circle must be seven by seven handbreadths, and what the circle has beyond the square does not combine at all. Just as according to Rabbi Yochanan in Sukkah 8a such a circle requires four amos by four amos, the same applies for us; see the Bach, of blessed memory. In Yoreh De'ah 286:13, and see Shach, letter 23, the Mechaber there ruled that what is at the sides in a circle does combine properly, and if among all of it there is enough there to square four amos, it is obligated in mezuzah even though there is not a square emerging from within the circle, like the Rambam there, unlike the Rosh, who held that there too we require an actual square emerging from within the circle. See the Magen Avraham here, letter 1, so that the words of the Shulchan Aruch should not be difficult from one place to another: here, regarding sukkah, we require that he sit with his head, most of him, and his table, and this is impossible without an actual square; by contrast, regarding sukkah of four amos by four amos, according to the Rambam of blessed memory, as understood by the Rosh and Beis Yosef, the total area through combination suffices. See there in the printed Magen Avraham: where it says "Rashi" it should read "the Bach"; and that is according to what the Rosh understood in the Rambam. It is not difficult why sukkah differs from mezuzah, as stated. See siman 631 in the Magen Avraham, letter 10, that seven by seven handbreadths is required at the height of ten handbreadths; this implies that everything must be squared, and sukkah decorations that reduce the space from the side likewise reduce seven by seven handbreadths from the side throughout the entire height of ten handbreadths. All these cases require analysis whether, by Torah law, a sukkah in such a case is invalid, or whether it is rabbinic. See siman 629 in the Magen Avraham, letter 22. See Gemara Sukkah 10b: "we are agents of a mitzvah and exempt from sukkah," and see Tosafos and Chiddushei HaRan there. It appears that according to the one who says that sukkah decorations that are distanced four handbreadths invalidate rabbinically, that is why they considered it a pressing circumstance and as if they had no other sukkah; therefore they sat there, and they also recited a blessing, according to what is written in Chiddushei HaRan regarding the statement that a time of danger is not a proof. But if it was invalid by Torah law, they would not have slept there, for what difference would there be in it? Alternatively, since it is a dispute, they were at least stringent upon themselves. Understand this, for there is a practical legal difference in this, as we have said.

turei_zahav.he: צריך שיהא בה כדי לרבע כו'. פירש ב"י דהיינו שיהא בה היקף כ"ט טפחים וב' חומשים וטעמו נ"ל דהא בעינן שיעור ז' על ז' במרובע כמ"ש . ובכל מרובע יש אלכסון דהיינו שני חלקים יותר מן הקו הפשוט כצ"ל בעיגול כי בעיגול אין שם אלכסון רק הקו הפשוט שבעיגול צריך שיהי' בו כמו בקו האלכסון שבמרובע והכי אמרי' בהדיא בגמ' דף ח' לר"י דס"ל שיעור סוכה ד' על ד' במרובע דבעי' בעיגול כשיעור קו אלכסון של מרובע ה"נ לדידן דשיעור סוכה בז"ט על ז"ט צריך שיהיה בקו העיגול כקו אלכסון של מרובע שהוא י"ט פחות חומש כי האלכסון יותר מהפשוט ב' חומשים וכיון שקו העיגול הוא י"ט פחות חומש ממילא ההיקף סביב העיגול הוא ג"פ כשיעור זה דכל שיש ברוחב טפח יש בהקיפו ג'. וע"כ צריך שיהיה בהיקף כאן ל' טפחים פחות מג' חומשים ובזה תוכל לעשות בו ריבוע ז' על ז'. אבל אם אין קו העיגול י"ט פחות חומש אלא פחות מזה אף אם הוא שתוכל לחתוך אותו לחלקים ויהי' שם מ"ט חלקים טפח על טפח דהיינו בקו של העיגול שהוא ח"ט ושמיני' טפח וההיקף הוא כ"ד טפחים שאז יש שם גם כן מ"ט חלקים כל אחד טפח על טפח כמ"ש מו"ח ז"ל בזה. מ"מ לא יהיו ברבוע באמצע העיגול כ"ט טפחים וב' חומשין ואז יש רבוע גמור בתוך העיגול ז' על ז' ודבריו בי"ד שזכרנו הם שלא בדקדוק ובין בסוכ' ובין במזוז' לעולם בעי' רבוע ממש כשיעור ולא ע"י צירוף החלקים לעשות מהם השיעור בין לרמב"ם בין להרא"ש אלא שהרא"ש לא נחית לפרש דברי הרמב"ם כן זה נ"ל ברור בס"ד:
turei_zahav.en: It must contain enough to square, etc. The Beis Yosef explained that this means that it must have a circumference of twenty-nine handbreadths and two fifths. His reason, it appears to me, is that we require the measure of seven by seven in a square, as I wrote. In every square there is a diagonal, meaning two parts more than the straight line; this must likewise be so in a circle, because in a circle there is no diagonal, only the simple line in the circle must be like the diagonal line in the square. And so we say explicitly in the Gemara on page 8 according to Rabbi Yochanan, who holds that the measure of a sukkah is four by four in a square, that in a circle we require the measure of the diagonal line of the square. So too according to us, where the measure of a sukkah is seven handbreadths by seven handbreadths, the line of the circle must be like the diagonal line of the square, which is nine handbreadths minus a fifth, for the diagonal exceeds the simple line by two fifths. Since the line of the circle is nine handbreadths minus a fifth, the circumference around the circle is automatically three times this measure, for anything that is one handbreadth wide has a circumference of three. Therefore the circumference here must be thirty handbreadths minus three fifths, and with this you can make within it a square of seven by seven. But if the line of the circle is not nine handbreadths minus a fifth, but less than this, even if it is possible to cut it into sections and there would be forty-nine sections there, each one a handbreadth by a handbreadth, namely with the line of the circle being eight handbreadths and one eighth of a handbreadth and the circumference being twenty-four handbreadths, for then there are likewise forty-nine sections, each one a handbreadth by a handbreadth, as my father-in-law, of blessed memory, wrote about this, nevertheless there will not be in the middle of the circle a proper square of seven by seven. And we require specifically squareness by the essence of the law. Now let us copy the words of the Beis Yosef in Yoreh De'ah, siman 286: "The Rosh wrote in the laws of mezuzah: Although in all the books it is written only, a house that does not have four amos is exempt from mezuzah, the Rif's text is: that does not have four amos by four amos, for it is reasonable that it is not fit for dwelling in any other manner. This is unlike the Rambam, who wrote that if its length was greater than its width, since it has four amos by four amos, it is obligated in mezuzah; for four amos by four amos is what we require for all those cases enumerated in the Baraisa in the first chapter of Sukkah." These are his words. And this is the language of the Rambam: "If it has enough to square four by four equally, even though it is round or five-sided, and needless to say if its length was greater than its width, since it has enough to square four by four, it is obligated in mezuzah." Regarding practical halachah, we adopt the Rambam's view, for only the Rosh disagrees with him, and the language "four amos by four amos" from which the Rosh learned is not decisive, for anything that contains enough to square four by four is included in four by four, since anything that contains enough to square thus is fit for dwelling. Until here is the language of the Beis Yosef in Yoreh De'ah. It is implied from the words of the Beis Yosef that he explains that according to the Rambam there, one does not need four by four in an actual square for mezuzah; rather, since it contains so much that one could make from it a square with four by four, that is enough. So too it appears that our master the Tur understood there, for he wrote: "The Rambam wrote that if it contains enough to square four by four, even though it is round, etc.; and my father, my master the Rosh, of blessed memory, wrote that it is not obligated unless it is square four by four." These are his words. I was very astonished at the covering of the eyes that I saw in our rabbis regarding this: how did the Rosh, and after him the Tur and Beis Yosef, understand from the Rambam's words that it does not need to be four in width and four in length? If so, why should it differ from sukkah here, where we require a square, as I wrote from the words of the Beis Yosef himself here, who gave the measure as twenty-nine handbreadths, as I wrote? Furthermore, what is the meaning of "equally" that the Rambam used, which would be unnecessary according to their understanding? Furthermore, why did the Rambam write "and needless to say if its length was, etc."? What obviousness is there in this more than in the first cases? The matter is clear that the Rambam also holds that we specifically require an actual square of four by four regarding mezuzah. That is why he used the language "equally"; he was careful that they not understand from his words that we do not require an actual square, but only that the circle contain so much that one could join and make a square. Rather, we specifically require that within the circle there actually be a square of four by four, without combining. But lest you ask: if so, it is obvious that it is obligated in mezuzah; therefore he wrote "even though it has no corners," to exclude the view of Acherim in the Gemara in the first chapter of Sukkah, who hold that a round sukkah is invalid because it has no corners, even though it has a square of the required measure within it. He teaches us that we do not rule so; rather, since it has an actual square equally within it, we are not concerned about corners. These are also the Rambam's words here regarding sukkah, and this is his language: "A round sukkah: if its circumference has enough to square seven by seven, even though it has no corners, it is valid." Thus he mentioned the novelty only regarding its lack of corners, implying that in any event it has the measure of length and width in an actual square. For if not, he should have written a greater novelty, namely, even though its length or width is not seven. Rather, it is obvious that we require an actual seven by seven in a square, and the only novelty here is from the aspect of the corner, to exclude Acherim whom we mentioned. This is also his intent regarding mezuzah: certainly the essential square requires four by four, but the novelty is from the aspect of the corner. And this is what he wrote, "and needless to say if its length was greater, etc.": meaning that it has there a length of five amos and a width of four amos; automatically there is at least an actual square of four by four, only there is an additional part in the length beyond the square. Because of this it is included in "not square," for every square has equal length and width. Nevertheless, if you cut off the excess length, you will have a complete square of four by four; it does not harm you that there is more than the fitting square. It emerges that according to the Rambam the law is also as the Rosh holds, that we require an actual square of four by four. But, with forgiveness due to the honor of the lights of our eyes, the Rosh and those who followed him did not intend this in their understanding of the Rambam's words; rather, they understood from his words that an actual square is not needed at all, and even if the length or width is less than the measure, it is valid. This never entered his mind. So too appears to be the view of the Maggid Mishneh, who wrote in Hilchos Sukkah that the Rambam who validates a round sukkah derives it from Rabbi Yochanan regarding a sukkah made like a kiln, etc.; and in the Gemara there it is proven according to Rabbi Yochanan that we require an actual square of four by four. Automatically, according to us too this is so regarding a sukkah whose measure is seven by seven, and as the Beis Yosef wrote here, that it requires a circumference of twenty-nine handbreadths and two fifths, so that there is a complete square inside the circle of seven by seven. His words in Yoreh De'ah that we mentioned are imprecise. Both regarding sukkah and regarding mezuzah, we always require an actual square of the measure, and not by combining the sections to make up the measure, whether according to the Rambam or according to the Rosh. It is only that the Rosh did not descend to explain the Rambam's words this way. This appears clear to me, with the help of Heaven.

פסולה - ועיין בש"ג בשם ריא"ז דכלי תשמישין אינו ממעט אפילו מן הצד והנה המגן אברהם העתיק דברי הש"ג לעיל בסימן תרל"ג סק"ז לענין אם תלויין ויורדין לתוך עשרה דחשיבי כמו נויין ולכאורה יותר רבותא היה אם היה מעתיקו לענין מן הצד דאף דנויין ממעטין כלי תשמישין אינו ממעט ומשמע מזה דלא פסיקא ליה למ"א דבר זה ולכן לא העתיקו וצ"ע ועיין בתר"ל סי"ג ולקמן סימן תרל"ט בט"ז סק"ג ובב"ח שם:

It from seven, etc. See Bach below, siman 639:3, who wrote the reason: since it is forbidden to remove it throughout all seven days. According to this, where one stipulated that he is not separating himself from it for the entire twilight period, so that it is permitted to remove it, as explained below, it does not reduce the measure. See Mishbetzos Zahav below, siman 639:3 [for he wrote there that this requires analysis]. Chiddushei Rabbi Akiva Eiger.
Is invalid. See Shiltei Gibborim in the name of Riaz, that utensils used for service do not reduce the measure even from the side. Now, the Magen Avraham copied the words of Shiltei Gibborim above in siman 633, small paragraph 7, regarding when they are hanging and descend into the space of ten, that they are considered like decorations.
